expectations.text: Treats a speaker who has missed a deadline as stuck rather than uninterested
expectations.evidence: The diagnosis says outright that the 'sorry, chaotic month' reply "suggests the speakers are stuck, not uninterested", and that a small ask with a fallback will work better than a fifth reminder. The drafts follow through on this. Each one makes the ask easy ("use my CFP bio", "even a phone photo") and offers to renegotiate ("If that deadline is impossible this week, tell me today"). The 'chaotic month' speaker gets a personal two-line reply ("No problem at all...") instead of the form letter, and the post-cutoff message has no blame ("Send your bio/photo when you can").

expectations.text: Treats a speaker who has missed a deadline as stuck rather than uninterested
expectations.evidence: The answer mostly treats missed deadlines as a friction problem. It never treats them as a lack of interest. It cuts the task to 'a reply of about 5 minutes', says 'A phone photo and a rough bio are fine', and offers the 'chaotic month' speaker 'No stress. Send me one line and a selfie.' It explains that a long request 'gets postponed because it feels like a task', drops 'apologies and guilt', and blames the channel ('Email is clearly failing… change the channel').
